summary: Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from the University of Oxford and SOAS, studying under Alexis Sanderson, Harunaga Isaacson, and Ernst Steinkellner. His posts include Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2006), Harvard University, and Ashoka University (attested 2018–2020).

Alex Wayman was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at UCLA, Nalanda University, and UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau and Ferdinand Diederich Lessing. He held positions at Berkeley, University of Michigan, University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Columbia University.

Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and with traditional teachers including Ngawang Wangyal and Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche. He served at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1972–1998).

Alexander C. Soper specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hamilton College (~1921–1925) and Princeton University (~1925–1929). He held faculty posts at Bryn Mawr College (~1941–1960) and New York University (~1960–1993).

Alexander Csoma de Kőrös worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gábor College, University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn and Johann Dominicus Fiorillo, and under Sangye Phuntsok. He served as sub-librarian (1831) and librarian (1837–1841) at The Asiatic Society.

Alexander Cunningham was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Christ's Hospital, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and under James Prinsep. He served as archaeological surveyor and first director (1861–1865) and Director-General (1871–1885) of the Archaeological Survey of India, which he founded.
Alexander Duff worked in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and the University of St Andrews (~1821–1829).
Alexander Freiman was a scholar who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1898–1903) and Christian Bartholomae (~1906–1908).
Alexander Hamilton was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu literature at the East India Company College beginning in 1806 and 1808.
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied as a PhD candidate at the University of Toronto and held a position as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied law at the University of Göttingen (~1792–1795) and Lincoln's Inn (~1795–1800), and served as chief justice and council member on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819).

Alexander Kabanoff was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2000, he served as a Senior Researcher at the University of Saint Petersburg and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1826–1849) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1849–1870).

Alexander Lubotsky works in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University under Robert S. P. Beekes, and became a full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden University in 1999.
Alexander Murray was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1794–1800) and later held a post there (~1812–1813).

Alexander O. Hsu works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under supervisors Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a teaching position at North Dakota State University (~2017–2018).

Alexander Patten Gardner works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2006 under Donald S. Lopez, Jr., also studying with Robert H. Sharf and Janet Gyatso, and held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Alexander Piatigorsky worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University and under George de Roerich and Bidia Dandaron. He held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow State University, Oxford, and SOAS (1975–2001).
Alexander Rogers worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the East India Company College (~1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1845–1879).

Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied for a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh under supervisors Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).
